verdict: Asana: Choose Asana when cross-functional teams need clear ownership, goals and workflows without an engineering-tracker learning curve. Scores use the project-management editorial methodology from first-party research as of 2026-08-17 — not hands-on product testing.
weaknesses: Can feel light vs monday for ops configurability
bestFor: Buyers prioritising adoption ease and goals/workflows
notIdealFor: Engineering sprint orgs that need Jira/Linear
Teams wanting the cheapest all-in-one seat (ClickUp)
tradeoffs: Seat minimums and AI credit bundles vs published per-seat floors
Work OS breadth vs specialist timeline / PDF / remote / desktop depth
Automation and reporting depth vs ease of use for small teams
Included AI credits vs paid AI add-ons or credit top-ups
recommendation: Choose Asana when cross-functional teams need clear ownership, goals and workflows without an engineering-tracker learning curve. Compare monday.com/ClickUp for Work OS configurability, Hive for lower SMB floors, and Jira/Linear if the buyer job is software delivery.
editorialNotes: Project-management Priority-1 batch. Approved on project-management-editorial v1.0.0. membershipRole=primary. jobCluster=work-os. handsOnTesting=false. Affiliate economics excluded.

criterionAssessments.rationale: Asana is repeatedly positioned for fast adoption by non-technical cross-functional teams — high ease vs engineering trackers.
Tasks, projects, timelines, portfolios and goals give a strong Work OS planning envelope peer to monday.com.
Rules and workflow builders are strong on Advanced+; Starter is lighter — held at 8 vs monday’s 9.
Comments, proofing-adjacent workflows and cross-team ownership are core strengths.
Broad native + Zapier ecosystem; slightly behind monday’s published breadth narrative.
Dashboards and goals reporting solid on Advanced; not a BI suite.
Clear Free → Starter → Advanced → Enterprise path for mid-market and up.
Starter $10.99 sits above ClickUp/monday Basic floors; capability justifies mid-market spend. Affiliate economics excluded.
AI Studio / Teammates marketed on paid tiers with credit packaging — strong capability with TCO friction.

overallScoreRationale: Weighted average of the nine project-management editorial criteria using the category weights (work planning 15, automation & workflows 14, ease of use 12, collaboration 12, integrations 12, reporting 10, value 10, scalability 9, AI 6), rounded to 1 decimal. Products are scored inside their job cluster — work OS / PM peers, timeline specialists, and adjacent PDF / remote-access / desktop-workspace tools are not forced into one undifferentiated ranking. Not a hands-on lab score, and affiliate economics are excluded.
